Here are our documents.

=== Notes ===
Sample (fictional)

Tallow Creek Respite Cooperative
Board meeting notes, Wednesday, November 4, 2026
Present: Osric Pellam (chair), Juniper Haldane (treasurer), Mirela Aske (executive director), Benedikt Orrin (program director)

Item 3: Ostrander Valley Health Fund

Mirela reported that Teodora Vance, program officer at the Ostrander Valley Health Fund, invited us to submit a short deck for their winter caregiving round after reading our FY2026 report. Ask: $120,000 for one year toward the FY2027 overnight respite pilot and the two eastern township workers. Total expansion cost is $165,000; the county Area Agency on Aging has already committed $45,000.

Deadline: deck to Teodora by Tuesday, December 1, 2026. Mirela wants a draft to the board by Friday, November 20.

Juniper noted that Fenwright's $150,000 does not renew at the same level after FY2027 and asked that we not hide how much we lean on the county and Fenwright (64 percent). Osric agreed.

Instructions for the deck, agreed by the board:
1. Keep it to eight slides or fewer. Teodora said she reads them on her phone.
2. Lead with the waitlist: 41 days down to 12. That is our strongest number and it is not in dispute.
3. Show the strain result (27.4 to 19.8) only with the caveat in plain view: 96 of 171 families answered, no comparison group, our own staff gave the survey. Do not call the program "evidence-based" and do not say respite keeps people out of nursing homes.

response.draft:
Slide 1: Tallow Creek Respite Cooperative
In-home respite for unpaid family caregivers
Marrow Junction and the Upper Tallow townships, since 2019
Request to the Ostrander Valley Health Fund, winter caregiving round
$120,000 for one year (FY2027)
Funds an overnight respite pilot and two respite workers in the eastern townships

Slide 2: Wait for a first visit: 41 days down to 12
Average days from referral to first visit: 41 in FY2025, 12 in FY2026
Families on the waitlist at year end: 37 down to 9
Emergency requests filled within 48 hours: 58% (29 of 50) up to 83% (62 of 75)
What changed: worker pay went from $16.50 to $19.00 an hour
Workers who left during the year: 11 of 23 in FY2025, 4 of 31 in FY2026
We also hired a second coordinator and moved scheduling off paper

Slide 3: What we do
Local workers come into the home and stay with an adult who needs supervision
Usually a parent or spouse living with dementia, Parkinson's disease or the after-effects of a stroke
While the worker is there, the caregiver can see a doctor, sleep or rest
FY2026: 171 families, 9,880 respite hours (FY2025: 118 families, 6,240 hours)
Sliding-scale fees from $0 to $14 an hour; 64% of families paid nothing
All-in cost per respite hour: $61.98, down from $68.40
94 cents of every dollar went to delivering or coordinating respite
"For two years I hadn't been to my own doctor. The first Tuesday [our respite worker] came, I went, and I found out I needed the surgery I'd been putting off." (caregiver, Upper Tallow township)

Slide 4: Caregiver strain: a promising result with limits
Measure: 12-item Zarit Burden Interview (scored 0 to 48; higher means more strain)
Average score at intake: 27.4. At six months: 19.8, a drop of 7.6 points
61 caregivers started in the high-strain band (17 or above); 34 of them were below 17 at six months
Read with care:
Only 96 of 171 families completed both surveys, and those who answered may have been doing better
There is no comparison group, and strain often eases for other reasons
Our own coordinators gave the survey
These numbers fit our belief that respite helps, but they do not prove the program caused the drop
FY2027: an outside evaluator will run follow-up surveys, and we will track why families leave

Slide 5: Two gaps we cannot fill today
Nights: 22 families asked for overnight coverage in FY2026, and we could not offer it
Dementia often means wandering, sundowning and lost sleep, and daytime visits do not help with that
Distance: Corliss and Harrow Flat townships made up 9% of referrals but only 4% of respite hours
A worker's round trip to the eastern townships can run 70 miles

Slide 6: FY2027 plan and how we will judge it
Pilot overnight respite for up to 40 families: two 9 p.m. to 7 a.m. shifts a month for six months
Hire two respite workers who live in Corliss and Harrow Flat
Train 14 current workers in dementia care (required for overnight shifts)
Bring in an outside evaluator for follow-up surveys and exit interviews
We will report three measures, even if the results disappoint:
Share of pilot caregivers with at least 5 nights of unbroken sleep a month
Six-month strain scores, collected by the outside evaluator
Whether families keep using the service

Slide 7: FY2027 expansion budget: $165,000
Two eastern township respite workers (2.0 FTE wages and benefits): $96,000
Overnight pilot shift pay (up to 40 families, 6 months): $38,500
Dementia care training for 14 workers: $12,800
Added rural mileage: $9,200
Independent evaluation: $8,500
Total: $165,000
Already committed: $45,000 from the Upper Tallow County Area Agency on Aging (part of the eastern township workers)
Remaining gap and our request: $120,000

Slide 8: Our finances, including our risks
FY2026 revenue: $618,900. Expenses: $612,400. Surplus: $6,500, added to reserve
Operating reserve covers about seven weeks of expenses
County Area Agency on Aging contract: $246,000 (40% of revenue)
Fenwright Family Foundation: $150,000 (24% of revenue)
Together, these two sources make up 64% of our revenue
The Fenwright grant ends its three-year term in FY2027 and will not renew at the same level
Other revenue: individual donors and the Porch Supper (14%), Marrow Junction Community Health Trust (12%), family fees (10%)
Contact: Mirela Aske, Executive Director
